cards.title: Empty Nest: Preparing for Your Child's University Years
cards.body: Sending your first child to university can trigger unexpected emotions, even when you intellectually understand it's a natural milestone. Parents often experience denial and grief about the separation before their child even leaves home.

cards.title: Second Baby Parenting: What You Actually Forget
cards.body: New parents of second children are often surprised by how much they've forgotten about feeding, teething, and sleep routines. Having family support and reflecting on your own childhood experiences can ease the transition.

cards.title: AI Parenting Tools: Do Your Kids Really Need Them?
cards.body: Tech companies are marketing AI-powered solutions like eye-movement trackers and nap predictors to overwhelmed parents. But the real question is whether optimization gadgets address what families actually need.

cards.title: The '18 Summers' Parenting Trend Explained
cards.body: The '18 summers' concept pressures parents to maximize every school holiday into memorable experiences. Simply allowing children unstructured downtime may be healthier than turning summers into curated memory-making exercises.

cards.title: Overparenting: When Helping Becomes Controlling
cards.body: Parenting becomes controlling when it prioritizes a parent's need to be needed over a child's growing independence. Healthy parenting balances connection with space for your child to grow and make mistakes.

cards.title: Back-to-School Without Cell Phones: Are Families Ready?
cards.body: More schools are implementing phone-free school days, and teens are adjusting to this new reality. Parents play a crucial role in supporting this transition and making it work at home too.

cards.title: After-School Meltdowns: Support for Neurodivergent Children
cards.body: Many neurodivergent children struggle with meltdowns or shutdowns after school due to emotional regulation challenges. Parents and schools can collaborate on strategies to help kids manage transitions across different environments.

cards.title: Empty Nest Feelings Begin Before Kids Actually Leave
cards.body: Parents often start grieving their child's departure emotionally before it physically happens, as anticipating separation triggers real sadness. Understanding that these feelings are normal can help you prepare and process this life transition.

cards.title: Motherhood, Mental Health, and Addiction Support Gaps
cards.body: Women face significant stigma and barriers when seeking mental health and addiction treatment, especially as mothers. Creating accessible, judgment-free care options is essential for supporting maternal wellbeing in 2026 and beyond.

cards.title: Donor Conception: Belonging, Identity, and Family Story
cards.body: Donor conception can bring both hope and fear around genetic identity and belonging within families. Understanding how genetic loss shapes attachment, identity, and family narratives helps parents support their children.

cards.title: Exercise and Mental Health in Young People
cards.body: Research on 38,000 children and adolescents shows exercise meaningfully improves depression and anxiety symptoms. Getting kids moving is one of the most evidence-backed strategies for supporting their mental health.

cards.title: IVF Mix-Up: Wrong Donor Sperm and Eggs in Cyprus
cards.body: Multiple families at a Northern Cyprus IVF clinic discovered they were given unintended donor sperm and eggs, raising serious questions about clinic protocols. This case highlights the need for strict verification systems in fertility treatment.

cards.title: Postpartum Psychosis: Mother Seeks Help Before Tragedy
cards.body: A mother experiencing postpartum psychosis begged for help before a tragic incident involving her children. Her case underscores the critical importance of recognizing postpartum mental health crises and providing immediate support.

cards.title: Salmonella Outbreak Linked to Imported Eggs
cards.body: A salmonella outbreak has sickened hundreds in the UK, primarily linked to contaminated imported eggs. Families should check egg sources and practice proper food safety to protect children and vulnerable household members.

cards.title: Young Adults Taking Anxiety Medication Instead of Alcohol
cards.body: Some young adults are taking prescription anxiety medications at parties as an alternative to drinking alcohol, dividing experts on health implications. This trend reflects changing attitudes about substance use but carries its own risks and ethical concerns.
